skill.name: clerk-cli
skill.description: Guide Clerk CLI operations for authentication, users, organizations, sessions, configuration, webhooks, and deployment verification.
skill.summary: Manage Clerk resources through documented CLI workflows, endpoint discovery, and mutation previews.
skill.author: clerk

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts reflect Markdown formatting, placeholder URLs, and expected Clerk authentication rather than malware. Predictable shared temporary files create real confidentiality and integrity risks. Semantic risks include unapproved host reruns, misleading target selection, mismatched production previews, unattributed sign-in tokens, and contradictory mutation guidance; no malicious exfiltration evidence was found.

remediation.issue: Clerk records and configuration use predictable shared temporary files.
remediation.suggestion: Create a private temporary directory with restrictive permissions, avoid existing paths and symlinks, and remove exported files after inspection.

remediation.issue: Host reruns are recommended without an explicit permission boundary.
remediation.suggestion: Require user approval and follow harness restrictions before host execution. Offer human-run commands when credentials or network access are unavailable.
Check credential provenance and the effective instance before mutations. Remove unintended environment overrides and confirm the resolved production or development target.

remediation.issue: The configuration PUT preview and production write target different instances.
remediation.suggestion: Use identical application, instance, credential source, and payload for preview and execution. Require explicit approval before the production write.

remediation.issue: The impersonation recipe offers a sign-in token without actor attribution.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer audited actor-token impersonation for debugging. Restrict sign-in tokens to authorized application flows and prohibit unattended production debugging with them.

remediation.issue: Confirmation guidance conflicts and mutation examples omit previews.
remediation.suggestion: Remove claims that --yes protects agent mutations. Add dry-run steps and explicit target verification to every supported mutation example.

semantic_findings.title: Host execution guidance omits the approval boundary
semantic_findings.description: The instruction "Rerun it on the host before acting on it or reporting it to the user" follows sandbox failures. Automatic compliance expands credential and network access without an explicit approval requirement.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Repeated instructions require host reruns after restricted execution fails, but do not require approval. Legitimate troubleshooting is plausible; deliberate malicious intent is not established.

semantic_findings.title: Explicit application flags may not control the actual credential target
semantic_findings.description: The safety advice recommends application flags, but CLERK_SECRET_KEY takes precedence over application resolution. An inherited production key can therefore defeat apparent development targeting.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented resolution order places the environment secret above application resolution. The same reference explicitly warns that local production keys select production.

semantic_findings.title: Production configuration write differs from the preview target
semantic_findings.description: The configuration recipe previews a PUT without an instance flag, then applies it with production selected. A development preview does not authorize full production replacement.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The adjacent commands show different targeting flags, and the reference states development is the default. The mismatch is directly observable in the recipe.

semantic_findings.title: Impersonation alternative removes actor attribution
semantic_findings.description: The recipe offers sign-in tokens for signing in "with no actor audit trail". It lacks explicit user authorization and production restrictions for this attribution-free alternative.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The recipe explicitly contrasts audited impersonation with unattributed sign-in tokens. Legitimate custom sign-in flows exist, but unrestricted debugging use creates an accountability risk.

semantic_findings.title: Conflicting mutation confirmation instructions
semantic_findings.description: One instruction says missing --yes causes confirmation errors, while the behavior matrix says agent mutations execute without prompts. Several mutation recipes also omit previews.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The reference makes directly contradictory claims about confirmation gates. Executable creation, update, ban, and membership examples lack dry-run steps despite the main safety rule.

content.user_title: Manage Clerk Resources with the CLI
content.value_statement: Clerk management tasks require correct authentication, endpoint discovery, and instance targeting. This skill guides CLI workflows for resource management, configuration, webhook testing, and deployment verification.
actual_capabilities: Guide OAuth login, platform-key authentication, accountless operation, and application linking.
Discover Backend and Platform API endpoints from the CLI catalog and invoke documented API operations.
List, create, and update users, organizations, memberships, invitations, and sessions through documented commands.
Inspect instance configuration, preview changes, synchronize environment keys, and toggle organizations or billing.
Set up local webhook relay listeners and verify saved delivery signatures offline.
Interpret deployment handoff reports and verify domain, SSL, email DNS, and OAuth readiness.
limitations: The bundle provides instructions, not a CLI implementation; compatible Clerk tooling must be available.
API access depends on credentials, account permissions, network connectivity, and the selected application or instance.
Deployment setup and unauthenticated OAuth login still require human interaction.
Agent mode skips most mutation confirmations; safe targeting, private exports, and explicit approval require additional care.

use_cases.title: Inspect development users
use_cases.description: Find development users, inspect selected fields, and prepare approved account changes without exporting complete records into chat.

use_cases.title: Verify production readiness
use_cases.description: Review deployment handoffs and check domain, SSL, email DNS, and OAuth status after a human completes production setup.

use_cases.title: Test webhook integrations
use_cases.description: Forward development webhook events to a local handler and verify captured signatures before debugging delivery processing.

prompt_templates.title: Check CLI health
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect my Clerk CLI version and health without changing resources. Summarize failures and request approval before host execution or credential changes.

prompt_templates.title: Find development users
prompt_templates.prompt: Find users matching [email] in development application [app_id]. Verify the effective credential target first and show only identifiers and matching status.

prompt_templates.title: Test local webhook delivery
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a development webhook listener for [local_handler_url]. Use private storage for captured events and verify signatures without exposing signing secrets.

prompt_templates.title: Preview a production configuration change
prompt_templates.prompt: Preview [configuration_change] for production application [app_id]. Verify credential precedence and use identical targets for preview and execution. Wait for explicit approval before writing.

output_examples.input: Check Clerk health without changing resources.
output: Authentication: unavailable in the current execution environment.
Project link: could not be verified.
No changes made. Host execution requires approval before repeating credential-dependent checks.

output_examples.input: Summarize this deployment report: domain DNS is complete, SSL is pending, and OAuth is ready.
output: Next action: repeat the read-only deployment status check after provisioning progresses.

output_examples.input: Preview a session lifetime change for the selected production instance.
output: Preview target: the explicitly selected production application and instance.
Proposed change: update the session lifetime.
No production write has been performed.

best_practices: Verify CLI help, credential provenance, and the effective application and instance before acting; environment secrets can override application flags.
Preview mutations with the same target and payload used for execution, then obtain explicit approval for production changes.
Keep secrets out of chat and repositories; protect exported records with private temporary storage and respect host execution permissions.
anti_patterns: Assuming --yes or agent mode provides a confirmation barrier for destructive operations.
Previewing development configuration, then applying the same payload to production without a production-specific review.
Exporting complete user records into shared temporary paths or using unattributed sign-in tokens for production debugging.

faq.question: Does this skill install or replace the Clerk CLI?
faq.answer: No. It documents CLI usage and package-runner options. Running commands requires compatible Clerk tooling and appropriate execution permissions.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: The bundle supports all three tools. Command execution still depends on the tool environment, shell access, credentials, and permissions.

faq.question: Do all operations require a Clerk account?
faq.answer: No. Supported accountless development flows use local keys. Application listing, linking, impersonation, and some configuration operations require account authentication.

faq.question: Does agent mode confirm destructive changes?
faq.answer: Most mutation confirmations are skipped. Use dry-run previews, verify the effective target, and obtain explicit approval before production writes.

faq.question: Can the skill test webhooks locally?
faq.answer: It documents a Clerk webhook relay, forwarding to a local handler, and offline signature verification. Captured events and signing secrets need protection.

faq.question: Can an agent complete production deployment alone?
faq.answer: No. The interactive setup wizard requires a human terminal. Agents can inspect handoff reports and verify readiness with deployment status checks.
